newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling firm, activity up marginally.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling firm, activity up marginally.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling firmed against the dollar on Friday as activity picked up marginally on a backlog accumulated from Thursday's strike by union bank employees, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 54.89 against the dollar from 54.92 while on the pound it was posted at 91.48 from 91.99.
On Thursday, dealers from banks whose processing departments employed unionisable staff said they were not transacting because there was no-one to process their orders.
Some dealers said they expected the shilling to remain within the 55.75/55 level as there was little trade incentive.
"Most companies are closing for the Christmas break today, and they won't reopen till after January 1," one dealer said.
The money market was a bit tight. Overnight rates were quoted at around 20 percent levels Thursday's 13-20 percent levels.
